title: 2014 AMC 12B Problem 9
statement: Convex quadrilateral \(ABCD\) has \(AB = 3,\) \(BC = 4,\) \(CD = 13,\) \(AD = 12,\) and \(\angle ABC = 90^\circ,\) as shown. What is the area of the quadrilateral?

solutions.text:
By the Pythagorean Theorem in right triangle \(ABC,\) \(AC = \sqrt{3^2+4^2} = 5.\)

Since \(5^2 + 12^2 = 13^2,\) the converse of the Pythagorean Theorem shows \(\angle DAC = 90^\circ,\) so \(\triangle DAC\) is right.

The area of \(\triangle ABC\) is \(\tfrac12\cdot3\cdot4 = 6\) and the area of \(\triangle DAC\) is \(\tfrac12\cdot5\cdot12 = 30.\) The quadrilateral has area \(6 + 30 = 36.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Use right triangle \(ABC\) to find diagonal \(AC\)
